articles.title: A couple claimed every dollar would save starving babies in Malawi; the charity founders diverted more than $2 million for cosmetic surgery, cruises and luxury holidays
articles.summary: Donors who supported an Arkansas charity were told their contributions would help feed and protect vulnerable babies in Malawi, one of the world's poorest
articles.body: Donors who supported an Arkansas charity were told their contributions would help feed and protect vulnerable babies in Malawi, one of the world's poorest countries. The organisation, called 2nd Milk, presented itself as a ministry where sponsorship money went towards children rather than the personal expenses of its founders. But an investigation into its finances uncovered a different use for the donations. According to the US Department of Justice, more than $2 million was diverted to cover expenses ranging from cosmetic surgery and massages to international holidays, cruises and household bills. The charity's founders, Jason Boyd Carney and his wife, Lacey Christina Carney, have now been sentenced to prison after their involvement in the scheme was established in federal court.Arkansas charity founders receive maximum prison sentences for $2 million fraudThe couple, who founded 2nd Milk in Springdale, Arkansas, were sentenced on October 14, 2026, in the Western District of Arkansas. Jason Carney received 192 months in federal prison, equivalent to 16 years, for offences connected to conspiracy, wire fraud and tax fraud. He will also serve three years of supervised release after completing his prison term.His wife, Lacey Carney, received a 36-month prison sentence for failing to report her husband's fraudulent activities despite knowing about the scheme. Her sentence also includes one year of supervised release. Federal prosecutors said both punishments represented the maximum prison terms permitted under the counts for which they were convicted.Reportedly, Chief US District Judge Timothy L. Brooks presided over the sentencing. In describing Jason Carney's actions, the judge used the words "profoundly disgusting", calling the conduct "egregious, repulsive, and violative". The sentences followed an investigation involving Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation and the Diplomatic Security Service.How 2nd Milk founders convinced donors their money was helping starving babiesFor several years, Jason Carney presented 2nd Milk as an organisation with a clear financial commitment to the children it supported. Its fundraising messages placed particular emphasis on transparency, with donors encouraged to believe that sponsorship contributions were being used for their intended purpose.The promises were unusually direct. Carney told potential supporters that all sponsorship money went towards saving vulnerable babies in developing countries. In another assurance, he said that 82 cents of every dollar went to babies, while the remainder covered overhead expenses in Africa. He also maintained that neither he nor his wife took money from people sponsoring children.Carney repeatedly insisted that he had never received a salary from the organisation. One of his assurances stated that all the money went specifically towards the children. Prosecutors later presented these statements as part of the evidence showing how donors had been persuaded to continue supporting the charity.The organisation's stated purpose was to help orphaned and malnourished children in Malawi. Supporters were therefore contributing on the understanding that their money would provide assistance to a particularly vulnerable group, rather than finance the personal lives of those running the organisation.Charity money paid for cosmetic procedures, cruises and overseas holidaysThe financial investigation uncovered payments that prosecutors said had little connection to 2nd Milk's charitable work. Bank records showed that money belonging to the nonprofit had been used to meet a range of personal expenses for Jason and Lacey Carney.Among the purchases and payments identified were cosmetic surgery, massages, tanning services and expenses involving their pets. Charity funds also went towards a cruise, mortgage payments on the couple's home, and loans connected to their cars and boat. Investigators also traced money used for luxury travel.The couple visited several international destinations, including Rome, Chile, Peru, Japan, Barcelona, Cancun and Vietnam. These trips were among the personal expenses that prosecutors linked to the diversion of charitable contributions.The misuse of donations was accompanied by efforts to conceal the financial activity. Prosecutors established that Jason Carney submitted false tax returns for himself and 2nd Milk, including an inaccurate annual nonprofit return, to hide the diversion of funds.Jason Carney admitted fraud and tax offences during his trialThe criminal proceedings included a jury trial, although Jason Carney changed his position before the prosecution had completed presenting its case. On the sixth day of the trial, he entered guilty pleas to four counts.These included conspiracy to commit wire fraud, two counts of filing false tax returns and one count of structuring cash transactions to avoid reporting requirements. The tax offences covered his personal return and the charity's Form 990, which nonprofits use to report financial and organisational information to the Internal Revenue Service.The structuring charge concerned the handling of cash transactions in a way intended to evade the reporting requirements that apply to certain financial activity. Together, the offences formed part of the case against him over the use of charity money and the concealment of its movement.Lacey Carney, aged 47, pleaded guilty to one count of misprision of a felony. The offence relates to knowing that a federal crime has been committed and deliberately failing to report it to the appropriate authorities. Prosecutors said she knew about her husband's wire fraud scheme but did not disclose it as required by law. Jason Carney was 48 at the time of the proceedings. Both defendants were held responsible for their respective offences, although the charges and sentences against them were different.Couple agreed to give up their homeThe financial consequences of the case also extended to the couple's property. Jason and Lacey Carney agreed to forfeit their home after authorities established that proceeds from the wire fraud had been used towards mortgage payments.The forfeiture formed part of the financial penalties connected to the criminal proceedings. It also reflected the extent to which money diverted from 2nd Milk had been used to support the couple's personal assets and living expenses.The case was announced by the US Attorney's Office for the Western District of Arkansas as part of a wider federal enforcement effort targeting fraud and tax-related offences. The Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division and IRS Criminal Investigation were among the agencies involved in the nationwide initiative.Federal officials respond to misuse of charitable donationsUS Attorney Kevin R. Holmes said the sentences demonstrated the consequences for people who use charitable organisations to obtain personal financial benefits. He said the Carneys had violated the confidence placed in them by donors whose contributions were intended to support vulnerable children.IRS Criminal Investigation Special Agent in Charge Donald "Trey" Eakins also addressed the case, pointing to the difference between what donors believed they were funding and how the money was actually spent. He said contributions intended to help malnourished and orphaned infants had instead been diverted towards personal expenses.Nicholas Collura, principal deputy assistant secretary for diplomatic security and director of the Diplomatic Security Service, said the case illustrated the damage caused when charitable causes are used for personal gain. The agency had worked with federal investigators to uncover the financial activity.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Democratic rights were curtailed but constitutionally': Sonia Gandhi reflects on Emergency
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi has accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government of causing significant
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi has accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government of causing significant damage to India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, expressing confidence that the country's electorate would eventually bring about a return to proper governance.In an interview with The Hindu, Sonia said the damage extended to the country's democratic fabric and institutions, adding that people were increasingly recognising the consequences of the government's actions."Over the last twelve years, great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions," she said.She expressed optimism about the country's political future, while acknowledging that restoring democratic institutions and governance would require considerable time and effort, even after the present government leaves office."Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems to health, and great effort from political parties. People are now beginning to be restless and recognising the damage. But I am optimistic, and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," she said.Sonia Gandhi on the 1975 EmergencyReflecting on the 1975 Emergency imposed by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi acknowledged that democratic rights had been curtailed during the 21-month period but said the decision was taken constitutionally."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed, and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.She also offered her perspective on the circumstances leading to the imposition of the Emergency, referring to violent protests, attacks on government offices and public transport, widespread unrest and calls for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders.Also read: Court allows more evidence in Sonia Gandhi voter list case"Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's (Indira Gandhi) point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.Sonia further noted that Indira Gandhi eventually recognised the situation, called for general elections in March 1977 and later publicly acknowledged and apologised for the excesses committed during the Emergency."Hindsight allows us to put things better in perspective. Let's not forget that it was Mrs Gandhi herself who came to recognise what was happening and called for the March 1977 election. And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.Meanwhile, the BJP hit back at Sonia Gandhi over her criticism of the central government, with Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal invoking the 1975 Emergency and questioning her remarks on democracy.Speaking to reporters in Bikaner, Rajasthan, Meghwal said Gandhi should also recall the period when democratic rights were curtailed, opposition leaders were jailed and journalists were silenced."The article makes certain observations regarding democracy. I would like to ask Sonia ji: does she not recall the period of 1975, when democracy was strangled? Thousands of senior leaders from various political parties were thrown into jail, and the voices of journalists were silenced. She ought to remember that era as well. In contrast, over the last 12 years, PM Modi has nurtured, flourished, and strengthened democracy, proclaiming to the entire world that India is the 'mother of democracy.' It is Prime Minister Narendra Modi who has emphatically declared that 'India is the mother of democracy,'" he said.Responding to the opposition's demand for a special parliamentary session, Meghwal said the government was ready for a debate and urged opposition parties to submit a proposal. He also referred to the Home Minister's remarks at a rally in Haryana, saying Parliament was the appropriate forum for such discussions."Our Home Minister provided a fitting response (to Rahul Gandhi) at a rally in Haryana, pointing out that the Constitution-makers designated Parliament as the proper venue for such debates. If the opposition wishes to engage in a discussion, let them put forward a proposal; we can certainly convene a special session—there is no issue with that. The Prime Minister has also expressed a similar sentiment. As for the suggestion that someone should act as a 'judge'—our democratic system already has a mechanism for this; the Speaker serves as the arbiter. What is new about this proposal? Why not simply debate? Who is stopping them? They have written requesting a special session; the government is prepared to call one. We are ready for a debate," he said.Reacting to Sonia’s article, Union Minister Giriraj Singh launched a sharp attack on her, questioning her remarks on democracy and making allegations about her and her son’s citizenship."Sonia Gandhi, may God grant you a long life. You have grown weary from trying to 'launch' your son. You speak of democracy? You should be ashamed... You lived in this country for 12 years without citizenship, and it is alleged that you even cast a vote. Questions are also being raised regarding your son's citizenship. Abandon these ambitions. Forget about a return in 10 years; the Congress will never return to power in this country. You haven't held power in nine different states for the last 40 years. Sonia Gandhi, from the very Congress party that imposed the Emergency and silenced the voices of the people, is talking about democracy. You and your son are trying to incite a civil war in India; that ambition, too, will never be fulfilled."Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'The Congress leader also spoke about her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, describing it as an account of how she grew to love her husband and former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's family and India, and how that connection eventually brought her into public life.In the interview, she said she had long been reluctant to share her personal story but eventually decided to write about the experiences that shaped her life and her decision to enter politics."I had no desire to talk about it for so long. But it is not only a love story between the two of us, but it's also the story of how I grew to love Rajiv's family and the country to which they belonged, and then I too came to belong in it. And of how this love brought me into public life, when I saw the purpose of all the sacrifices they had made being threatened, and the party was weakening. I felt I had to do something," she said.The memoir traces Sonia's journey from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi, which brought her to India, to the personal losses that shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country. It also recounts her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her journey from private life to public service.The book, her first memoir, is scheduled to be launched on November 10.Rahul Gandhi expresses pride over mother's memoirEarlier, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had expressed his excitement over the publication of his mother's memoir, saying he was proud that her personal story would reach readers.On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, Rahul said he understood how difficult it had been for his mother, who preferred to maintain a private life, to share her experiences publicly."I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia," Rahul Gandhi said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Netanyahu planned Iran attack before Israel polls; operative's mistaken tip to US stopped it: Report
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Mossad chief Roman Gofman reportedly sought to launch an operation against Iran just before Israel's October
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Mossad chief Roman Gofman reportedly sought to launch an operation against Iran just before Israel's October 27 election, but the plan was stopped after the United States was alerted.The proposed operation was said to be opposed by senior officials in Israel's security establishment. They feared it could trigger a major escalation with Iran and disrupt the election. Despite these concerns, preparations for the unspecified operation continued. However, a mistake by an Israeli security operative reportedly tipped off Washington about the plan. The US then moved quickly to prevent the operation from going ahead, Channel 12 reported, as quoted by Times of Israel.Netanyahu's office rejected the report, saying: “The prime minister himself clarified in real time that an attack before the Israeli elections was not on the agenda.”The latest report follows a series of accounts in Israeli media about tensions between Netanyahu and senior military officials over possible action against Iran in the run-up to the election.Also read: Iran rebuilding missile sites, moving military infrastructure underground to evade strikesOn October 25, Channel 12 reported an “unprecedented confrontation” between Netanyahu and Israel Defence Forces (IDF) Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir over an order for unspecified military action. According to that report, Zamir resisted carrying out the instruction, sought further deliberations and asked Netanyahu to provide written authorisation for the move.Military officials were concerned that the proposed action could trigger a wider confrontation with Iran at a sensitive moment. The report also cited concerns that the political leadership could be seeking to use the Iran issue for electoral advantage.Netanyahu dismissed the account as “nonsense” in an interview with Channel 14, saying there had been “no fight” with Zamir. He had separately said he had instructed the IDF and Mossad to topple the Iranian regime.A day later, Channels 12 and 13 reported that Zamir was the only senior Israeli security chief opposing military action sought by Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz, amid fears it could escalate tensions with Iran and derail the election.Also read: 'Israel, Middle East wouldn't exist today': Trump boasts of stopping Iran's nuclear ambitionsIran talks complicate Netanyahu's push for strikesThe reported attempt to launch an operation comes amid diplomatic efforts to end the conflict between the US and Iran, with Qatar mediating negotiations. US President Donald Trump has indicated that he wants to give diplomacy more time, even as the possibility of renewed military action remains.Channel 12 reported earlier this week that Netanyahu had urged Trump to resume the war against Iran immediately after the US midterm elections. Trump, however, reportedly wanted Israel to avoid disrupting negotiations with Tehran.Netanyahu is said to be concerned that a diplomatic agreement could lead to a significant easing of pressure on Iran.Asked about Iran outside the White House on Friday, Trump said, “We've beaten Iran. We are doing very well with Iran. We're talking to Iran. We haven't lost a soldier in six or seven months.”He also repeated his claim that Israel and the wider Middle East would not exist today had he not stopped Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.The latest Channel 12 report marks a second alleged instance in which Washington intervened to prevent Israeli military action against Iran. The Financial Times had earlier reported that Trump opposed a separate Israeli plan for a more extensive offensive, which was reportedly ready to be launched on October 10.You use AI every day.
